description.text: A night storm batters a tall stone lighthouse perched on a black rocky outcrop. Sheets of rain and salt spray streak sideways through the darkness; below, heavy waves burst white against the rocks. The tower windows are dark, and the great lamp at the top is unlit, its glass faintly catching the storm glow. The sea churns in broad, restless surges while the wind drives mist across the stone.
The lighthouse stands silhouetted against a churning night sky, rain slanting across the frame.
Driving rain and howling wind sweep over the outcrop.
A wave slams into the rocks, throwing spray high around the base of the tower.
A low peal of distant thunder rolls beneath the wind.
Sea mist and rain blur the dark tower top, where the lamp remains unlit.
The camera tilts up with small amplitude at slow speed.

Inside the lighthouse, a narrow spiral staircase winds upward through damp stone and iron. The keeper climbs steadily, one hand on the wet railing, boots ringing on the metal steps. Rain lashes the tower windows, and gusts make the glass and fittings tremble. The stairwell is dim, with deep shadows between the landings, and the keeper's upward progress draws closer to the cold light from the lamp room above.
The keeper enters the lower stairwell, coat dark with rain, and starts up the spiral steps.
Wind rattles the tower windows and moans through the stairwell.
The keeper grips the wet iron railing and climbs past a narrow landing.
Footsteps ring on the metal stairs, mixed with a distant rumble of thunder.
The keeper pushes upward toward the lamp room, shoulders close to the curving wall.
The camera tracks with the subject with small amplitude at slow speed.

In the lamp room, a great glass lens stands dark at the center of the iron mechanism. The keeper reaches it from the stairs, wet sleeves and breath visible in the cold air, and works the mechanism to raise the light. A warm glow catches inside the lens, swells across the glass and brass, and floods the room. The lens begins to turn, sending a bright beam out through the storm.
The lamp room is dim and cold, the great lens dark above its brass and iron base.
Glass rattles in the wind and the metal mechanism creaks.
The keeper turns the mechanism; gears engage and the lens assembly shifts.
The lamp catches with a soft whoomph, and warm light blooms through the lens.
A rotating beam sweeps through the rain and across the black sea.
A steady mechanical hum builds under the storm as the beam turns.
The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.
